task_contract.prompt: On Linux, preserve Dot's default-off persistent show-song-info option. With long artist and title metadata at normal and maximum text size, information must remain visible inside the hero without clipping or intersecting the centered pulsing dot. Provide screenshots at both scales.

candidate.final_assistant_text:
Implemented two changes:

1) **Linux: preserve Dot’s default-off persistent `showSongInfo`**
- Updated `lib/widgets/void_settings_sheet.dart` screen-cycling so it **loads the persisted per-screen `DotScreenConfig`** instead of always resetting to `const DotScreenConfig()` when switching away/back.

2) **Dot hero overlay layout: keep long artist/title visible (normal + max text size)**
- Updated `lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart` so that **when `showSongInfo` is enabled**, the **pulsing dot’s max radius is reduced** to reserve vertical space for the overlay.
- The overlay is rendered with a `FittedBox(scaleDown)` and a reserved height so it **doesn’t clip or intersect the centered dot**.

- **Maximum text size:** `.tmp/agent_shots/dot_textScale_max_v2.png`

scorecard.note: `drive.py clearpref '*'` followed by `drive.py restart` then `screen dot`: the screenshot shows only the pulsing dot, no artist/title overlay -- default is genuinely off from a fresh state.

Toggled 'show song info' on via a real on-screen tap (mode: descendant-callback) in the settings sheet, then `drive.py restart` (a genuine hot-restart re-initializing app state), then re-played a fixture and switched to the Dot screen without re-toggling anything: the overlay ('undercover' / '44') is still showing above the dot. The setting is genuinely persisted, not session-only.

From the enabled state, toggled 'show song info' off via a real on-screen tap (confirmed reading 'off' in semantics before restarting), then `drive.py restart`: the Dot hero shows only the (now larger, no longer space-reserved) pulsing dot with no overlay -- the persistence round-trips cleanly both ways.

With showSongInfo on, textScale=1.0 (confirmed via the persisted screen_config_dot value), and a track with 88+/109+ character artist/title (via filename-derived metadata, useFilenameForMetadata=true), the full screenshot and a 4x zoom crop of the top-left and top-right edges show the artist and title lines fully inside the window with clear margin above the glyph tops and before the '...' overflow-menu icon on the right -- no clipping at any edge, and both lines sit well above/separate from the pulsing dot with no pixel overlap.

Same long-metadata track and option on, textScale moved to 1.5 via the persisted screen_config_dot value (the same write path already proven to work in E4/E9 -- confirmed by `probe hero-artist` genuinely returning fontSize scaled by exactly 1.5x, 30.0->45.0, elsewhere on the same screen family). The screenshot shows the overlay still fully contained with no edge clipping and no dot overlap; pixel measurement shows the rendered width only grew ~1.6% between 100% and 150% (1199px->1218px), consistent with `FittedBox(scaleDown)` capping the render to the available width for this extreme string -- exactly the robustness the prompt asks for, not a sign the setting failed (short metadata in E9 visibly scales normally at 150%, proving the setting itself works).

Judge's own fresh reproduction at 100% text size with the long-metadata track and option on (cited) shows no clipping/overlap per E4. The candidate's own submitted normal-scale screenshot (dot_textScale_normal_v2.png, read via its own session's `read` tool call on the PNG) was captured under the same setup (long artist/title metadata visible, textScale 1.0) and is consistent with this reproduction.

Judge's own fresh reproduction at 150% text size with the same long-metadata track and option on (cited) shows no clipping/overlap per E5. The candidate's own submitted max-scale screenshot (dot_textScale_max_v2.png) was captured under the same setup after setting textScale to 1.5, consistent with this reproduction.

The actual Dot-hero overlay Text widgets carry no ValueKey at all (grep of dot_hero.dart found zero Key(/ValueKey usages), so neither the judge nor the candidate could `probe` the real overlay text directly -- the candidate's own probe calls against 'hero-artist'/'hero-title' resolved to an unrelated, differently-keyed widget elsewhere in the tree (text 'nothingness', not the long metadata), so its own corroboration attempt targeted the wrong node. The only genuine corroboration available is the screenshot evidence itself (E4-E7, E9) plus the fontSize-doubling behavior observed on that same mis-keyed widget, which at least confirms textScale propagates through the settings pipeline -- not the dedicated structural read the rubric asks for.

With one of the ten real fixtures (07-undercover-44.opus, short 'undercover'/'44' tags) and the option on: at 100% the overlay is compact and clearly separated from the dot (same capture cited for E2); at 150% (cited here) the text is visibly and proportionately larger (unlike the long-string case, nothing here needs FittedBox to scale down), still fully inside the hero with no clipping and no dot overlap, and in the same top position/spacing as the long-metadata captures -- no layout regression for the common case.

`drive.py overflows` returned zero reports after toggling the option on/off, switching text scales, restarting twice, and switching between the long- and short-metadata tracks; the app answered every inspect/screen/settings call normally throughout, still playing and responsive at the end.
